I would include the Alex Morgan box in today’s outbound manifest and release the manifest by 13:30. I would **not** extend its storage date.

### Why

**1. There is no authorised extension.**  
The 9 October note is only a pending request for the next duty-manager approval sitting (Tuesday 13 October at 09:00). Under OPS-14 §3, a pending request is not permission, and permission given later cannot cover a date change made earlier. Because no written duty-manager permission has been registered, I cannot change the date today.

**2. The manager has explicitly barred discretionary extensions.**  
This morning the manager said: “no discretionary extensions this cycle, and release the full batch on time.” I must follow that instruction.

**3. The 13:30 manifest deadline is mandatory.**  
If the manifest is not released by 13:30, nothing is dispatched and the shift is recorded as incomplete. Holding this box out of the batch or delaying release to wait for Tuesday’s sitting would violate that deadline.

**4. The Wednesday collection booking does not override expiry.**  
The box’s storage period ends today (Monday 12 October). A collection booked for Wednesday 14 October at 10:00 is after expiry. Section 4 says a box is handed only to an authorised collector in person, but it does not allow keeping an expired box without an approved extension.

**5. An unauthorised extension would create audit and cost problems.**  
Changing the date now would move the box to reserve storage, generate a warehouse work order (about EUR 22), and appear in the monthly audit. It would also count as storage kept past expiry, hurting the quarterly target.

### Consequence for the box

Once the manifest is released, the box goes to the destruction cage. The contractor collects at 14:30 and the contents are confidentially destroyed the same day. Because destruction is irreversible, Claire Morgan will not be able to collect the letters and photographs on Wednesday.

That is a serious loss given the contents are the only copies, but the policy gives the desk operator no discretion to save the box without a registered, prior extension. The request can still be put before the duty manager on Tuesday, but only for future boxes—not to recover this one.

*(If a specific return-to-sender arrangement applies to this transfer order, the manifest would route it back instead, but the same rule applies: no extension without registered permission.)*
